1.explanation:
• ComposedModal/ComposedModal.js & ComposedModal/index.js: contain the implementation of the ComposedModal component, including the conditional that sets the button kind to ‘tertiary’ when danger=true.
• Modal/Modal.js & Modal/ModalFooter.js: define the base Modal and its footer button logic, showing how the ‘danger’ prop maps to the ‘secondary’ kind for the cancel button in the plain Modal.
• Button/index.js & Button/Button.js: provide the core Button component and its ‘kind’ prop handling and styles (primary, secondary, tertiary, danger). Reviewing this reveals how each kind is styled and helps diagnose why ‘tertiary’ and ‘secondary’ differ.
1.bug_scenario: The user is seeing inconsistent styling for the “Cancel” button when using the `danger` prop on the base `Modal` versus the `ComposedModal`. In the first screenshot (Modal with danger=true), the left button (“Cancel”) is rendered with the “secondary” style (a grey background with dark text). In the second screenshot (ComposedModal with danger=true), the left button is rendered with the “tertiary” style (a light grey/ghosted background) instead of the expected “secondary” look. This mismatch is due to a conditional in the ComposedModal source: `kind={danger ? 'tertiary' : 'secondary'}`. The user expects the cancel button to use the same “secondary” (grey) styling in both components when `danger=true`, but ComposedModal is defaulting to `tertiary`.
